source.note: Generated by `pnpm --filter @atlantis/ruleset scrape`. The movement, items and skills blocks are scraped from the URLs above; each movement value records the sentence it came from. Re-run the fetch rather than hand-editing, unless you are deliberately overriding a value.

provenance.movementPoints: Walking units have two movement points, riding units have four, and flying units have four
provenance.terrainCosts: Moving from one region to another normally takes one movement point, except that the following terrain types take two movement points for riding or walking units to enter: Forest, Mountain, Swamp, Jungle, and Tundra.
provenance.road: If a road in the given direction is connected, units move along that road at half cost to a minimum of 1 movement point
provenance.ocean: Units may not move through ocean regions without using the SAIL order unless they are capable of flight, and even then, flying units must end their movement on land or else drown
provenance.sailing: For a fleet to enter any region only costs one movement point. A coastal region is defined as a non-ocean region with at least one adjacent ocean region

risk.note: Chosen by Atlantis HUD, not scraped from the game. A hex is medium risk once hostile strength reaches mediumRatio times our own, and high risk at highRatio.

weather.note: The rules page states no weather rule, but implies one: winter raises the cost of at least mountain terrain above a walker's two movement points, by an amount the page never gives.
weather.consequence: A route crossing a winter month is under-cost, so a journey can look achievable when it is not. Present such a route as a lower bound rather than as fact.
weather.evidence: a unit on foot trying to move into a mountain region in winter would not have enough movement points to enter in one turn
